question: When does the GENIUS Act take effect, and are any of its rules final?
answer: The GENIUS Act takes effect on January 18, 2027. As of October 21, 2026, 1 of its rules is final and 12 are still proposals.
effective_date_rule: The Act takes effect on the earlier of January 18, 2027 (18 months after enactment) or 120 days after the primary regulators issue final implementing rules. No final rule existed by September 20, 2026 (120 days before January 18, 2027), so any later final rule lands after January 18 and the effective date is January 18, 2027.

rows.what: GENIUS Act signed into law
rows.detail: Public Law 119-27. Senate passed it 68-30 on June 17, 2025; House 308-122 on July 17, 2025.

rows.what: Treasury asks the public how to implement the Act (advance notice)
rows.detail: Advance notice of proposed rulemaking; comment period extended on October 1, 2025. Questions only, no rule text.

rows.what: FDIC proposes how its banks apply to issue stablecoins through a subsidiary
rows.detail: Comment period extended to May 18, 2026 (FIL-4-2026, February 6, 2026).

rows.what: NCUA proposes licensing for credit-union stablecoin subsidiaries
OCC proposes its core rule for the issuers it supervises
rows.detail: Capital, liquidity, reserves, governance and supervision. Comments closed May 1, 2026. This is the rule the OCC says it will finalize first. Finalized October 21, 2026 (see the OCC final-rule row).

rows.what: Treasury report on new ways to detect illicit digital-asset activity (section 9(e))
rows.detail: Located: a 34-page March 2026 report. It answers section 9(e) only; it is not the separate section 14 study.

rows.what: Treasury proposes the test for when a state's stablecoin regime is 'substantially similar' to the federal one
rows.detail: Section 4(c).

rows.what: FDIC proposes requirements and standards for the issuers it supervises
rows.detail: Includes deposit-insurance treatment of reserve deposits and tokenized deposits. FDIC Chairman Hill said in October 2026 that a final rule is being prepared.

rows.what: FinCEN and OFAC propose anti-money-laundering and sanctions programs for issuers
NCUA proposes issuance rules for credit-union-affiliated issuers
rows.detail: Supplements its February licensing proposal.

rows.what: FDIC proposes Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions standards for its issuers
OCC proposes weekly and quarterly reporting forms for issuers
rows.detail: Paperwork notice, not a rule.

rows.agency: FinCEN with OCC, Fed, FDIC and NCUA
rows.what: Five agencies propose customer-identification programs for issuers
OCC proposes anti-money-laundering and sanctions programs for its issuers
Three reports to Congress due: the section 14 study of non-payment stablecoins, the section 4(a)(6)(C) lawful-order report and the first section 15 industry report
rows.detail: No public text located. That does not prove they were not delivered: committee reports can be posted later.

rows.what: Deadline for final implementing rules (one year after enactment)
rows.detail: Passed with no final rule from any agency.

rows.what: FDIC publishes reporting forms for its issuers
rows.detail: Paperwork notice, not a rule.

rows.what: Treasury proposes the rules on who may issue, offer and sell stablecoins in the U.S. (section 3)
rows.detail: 87 questions for comment. Comments due October 19, 2026.

rows.what: Fed proposes how its member banks apply to issue stablecoins through a subsidiary (R-1900)
rows.detail: Published September 29; comments due November 30, 2026.

rows.what: Fed proposes reserve, capital and redemption standards for the issuers it supervises (R-1899)
rows.detail: Announced September 24; published September 29; comments due November 30, 2026.

rows.what: Treasury's procedure for certifying state regimes takes effect, but intake is closed
rows.detail: Interim final rule, effective September 30; comments due November 30. Treasury will not accept certifications until the paperwork approval comes through and it posts an acceptance notice. No state has been certified.

rows.what: Comments due on Treasury's section 3 proposal
OCC finalizes its GENIUS rule for the issuers it supervises
rows.detail: Effective January 18, 2027. Applications and transition waivers still await paperwork (OMB) approval and a separate OCC opening notice. Read in full (721 pages) in the GENIUS implementation package, October 21, 2026.

rows.what: OCC's stated target for its first final rule
rows.detail: Comptroller Gould, October 15, 2026: final rule expected before the end of October (earlier target was November). A target is not a rule. Met: the OCC released its final rule on October 21, 2026.

rows.what: Comments due on both Fed proposals (R-1899 and R-1900)
Comments due on Treasury's state-certification procedure
The Act takes effect
rows.detail: The earlier of January 18, 2027 or 120 days after final rules. With no final rule by September 20, 2026, January 18, 2027 controls. It takes effect even if the rules are still proposals.

rows.what: Digital-asset service providers may no longer offer or sell stablecoins that are not permitted payment stablecoins
rows.detail: Three years after enactment.

catalog_context.title: OCC final stablecoin rules: issuer duties, permissions and operating evidence
catalog_context.answer: The OCC's final GENIUS rule takes effect January 18, 2027. Its requirements attach to specific issuers, claims and custody relationships; approval, backing, capital, reporting and completed redemption require separate evidence.
